advices.diagnosis: The OrderService class is a classic god class: it has 26 public methods, a cyclomatic complexity of 56, and a cohesion of 5 components, indicating that its responsibilities are scattered across order lifecycle, pricing, audit, and notification. The high LCOM4 and NOM metrics show that the class is handling many unrelated concerns, while the DCC of 4 shows it is tightly coupled to several domain collaborators. This design violates the Single Responsibility Principle and makes the class hard to maintain, test, and evolve.

suggestions.title: Extract domain concerns into dedicated services

advices.risk_notes: Splitting the class increases the number of types in the module, which may raise the overall project DCC if the wiring code is duplicated. Care must be taken to avoid re‑introducing shared state (e.g., the audit log) across services. The refactor also requires updating all call sites and tests, which can be error‑prone. If the application is heavily coupled to the original OrderService API, the migration cost may outweigh the cohesion benefits.
